The evidence supports the claim the clearest instruction makes. Al-Husayn ﵇, in the reports, hears the visitor who stands at his grave, knows him, prays to Allah for him, and can be asked to pray for his need. The Prophet ﷺ and the Imams ﵈, in the reports, are alive with their Lord, aware of the deeds of the living, and receiving knowledge that arrives from Allah. The reports do not give the dead independent power. The effects they seek are sought from Allah, by the prayer of the one addressed. The Sunni canon carries the same structure in texts its scholars graded. That removes the assumption that the practice was invented by the Shia against the rest of the tradition.

The chains keep their limits, the isnad-less formula, the shared al-Asamm relay, the ungraded Ibn al-Jarish route, and the contested continuation relay, all printed above. None of this weakens the reports as witnesses of what the two traditions teach. All of it matters if the argument is pressed from attribution to authentication, a step this survey does not take.

What remains unsettled is the body, and the corpus itself is the reason, its reports divide and its own surveyors argue. The practice of asking rests on the hearing and the intercession, and the three-day report itself carries the greetings reaching them from far away and heard from near.

I have indeed been disappointed because of what has preceded from me.

quotes.caption: Imam al-Sadiq to Abd Allah ibn Bukayr, in Ibn Qulawayh, Kamil al-Ziyarat, p. 206

paragraphs.text: حدثني أبي ﵀ ، عن الحسين بن الحسن بن ابان ، عن الحسين بن سعيد ، عن عبد الله بن المغيرة ، عن عبد الله بن عبد الرحمان الأصم ، عن عبد الله بن بكير الأرجاني . وحدثني أبي ﵀ ، عن سعد بن عبد الله ، عن محمد بن الحسين ، عن محمد بن عبد الله بن زرارة ، عن عبد الله بن عبد الرحمان الأصم ، عن عبد الله بن بكير ، قال : حججت مع أبي عبد الله (﵇) - في حديث طويل - فقلت : يا بن رسول الله لو نبش قبر الحسين بن علي (﵉) هل كان يصاب في قبره شي ، فقال : يا بن بكير ما أعظم مسائلك ، ان الحسين (﵇) مع أبيه وأمه وأخيه في منزل رسول الله (﵌) ومعه يرزقون ويحبرون ، وانه لعن يمين العرش متعلق به يقول : يا رب أنجز لي ما وعدتني ، وانه لينظر إلى زواره وانه أعرف بهم وبأسمائهم وأسماء ابائهم وما في رحالهم من أحدهم بولده ، وانه لينظر إلى من يبكيه فيستغفر له ويسأل أباه الاستغفار له ويقول : أيها الباكي لو علمت ما أعد الله لك لفرحت أكثر مما حزنت وانه ليستغفر له من كل ذنب وخطيئة (2) .

My father related to me from al-Husayn ibn al-Hasan ibn Aban, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Abd Allah ibn al-Mughira, from Abd Allah ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Asamm, from Abd Allah ibn Bukayr al-Arjani. My father also related to me from Sa'd ibn Abd Allah, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Abd Allah ibn Zurara, from Abd Allah ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Asamm, from Abd Allah ibn Bukayr, who said,
"I made the pilgrimage with Abu Abd Allah, in a lengthy report. I said, 'Son of the Messenger of God, if the grave of al-Husayn ibn Ali were excavated, would anything be found in his grave?'

He said, 'O Ibn Bukayr, how grave your questions are. Al-Husayn is with his father, his mother, and his brother in the abode of the Messenger of God. With him they are provided for and made joyful. He is at the right of the Throne, clinging to it, saying, "My Lord, fulfill for me what You promised me." He looks upon those who visit him. He knows them, their names, the names of their fathers, and what is in their baggage better than any one of them knows his own child. He looks upon the one who weeps for him, asks forgiveness for him, asks his father to seek forgiveness for him, and says, "O you who weep, if you knew what God has prepared for you, you would rejoice more than you grieved." He seeks forgiveness for him for every sin and wrongdoing.'

quotes.caption: The second version of the Ibn Bukayr report, Kamil al-Ziyarat, pp. 543-544

paragraphs.text: قلت : جعلت فداك أخبرني عن الحسين (﵇) لو نبش كانوا يجدون في قبره شيئا ، قال : يا بن بكير ما أعظم مسائلك الحسين (﵇) مع أبيه وأمه وأخيه الحسن في منزل رسول الله (﵌) ، يحبون كما يحبي ويرزقون كما يرزق ، فلو نبش في أيامه لوجد (4) ، واما اليوم فهو حي عند ربه ينظر إلى معسكره ، وينظر إلى العرش متى يؤمر ان يحمله ، وانه لعلى يمين
I said, "May I be made your ransom, tell me about al-Husayn. If his grave were opened, would they find anything in it?"

He said, "O son of Bukayr, how grave your questions are. Al-Husayn is with his father, his mother, and his brother al-Hasan in the abode of the Messenger of God. They are granted gifts as he is granted them, and are provided for as he is provided for. If his grave had been opened in his days, he would have been found. But today he is alive with his Lord. He looks upon his camp, and he looks upon the Throne, awaiting when he will be commanded to bear it. He is clinging to the right side of the

quotes.caption: The second version, continued, Kamil al-Ziyarat, p. 544

paragraphs.text: العرش متعلق ، يقول : يا رب انجز لي ما وعدتني . وانه لينظر إلى زواره وهو اعرف بهم وبأسماء آبائهم وبدرجاتهم وبمنزلتهم عند الله من أحدكم بولده وما في رحله ، وانه ليرى من يبكيه فيستغفر له رحمة له ويسأل أباه الاستغفار له ، ويقول : لو تعلم أيها الباكي ما أعد لك لفرحت أكثر مما جزعت ، فيستغفر له كل من سمع بكائه من الملائكة في السماء وفي الحائر ، وينقلب وما عليه من ذنب (1) .
Throne, saying, "My Lord, fulfill for me what You promised me."

He looks upon his visitors, and he knows them, their fathers' names, their ranks, and their standing before God better than any one of you knows his own child and what is in his saddlebag. He sees whoever weeps for him, so he seeks forgiveness for him out of mercy for him, and asks his father to seek forgiveness for him. He says, "O weeper, if you knew what has been prepared for you, you would rejoice more than you grieve." Everyone who hears his weeping among the angels in heaven and in al-Ha'ir seeks forgiveness for him. He returns with no sin upon him.

quotes.caption: The dead believer and his visitor, al-Kafi, vol. 3, p. 232

paragraphs.text: 4 - عدة من أصحابنا ، عن عن إسحاق بن عمار ، عن أبي الحسن (﵇) قال : قلت له : المؤمن يعلم بمن يزور قبره ؟ قال : نعم ولا يزال مستأنسا به ما دام عند قبره فإذا قام وانصرف من قبره دخله من انصرافه عن قبره وحشة .

4 - A number of our companions, from Ishaq ibn Ammar, from Abu al-Hasan, who said, "I said to him, 'Does a believer know who visits his grave?' He said, 'Yes. He remains comforted by him as long as he is at his grave. When he rises and departs from his grave, loneliness enters him because of his departure from his grave.'"

quotes.caption: Ali ibn Abi Talib, relayed by al-Sadiq, al-Kafi, vol. 3, p. 234

paragraphs.text: وعن عبد الله بن عبد الرحمن الأصم ، عن حريز ، عن محمد بن مسلم ، عن أبي عبد الله (﵇) قال : قال أمير المؤمنين (﵇) زوروا موتاكم فإنهم يفرحون بزيارتكم وليطلب أحدكم حاجته عند قبر أبيه وعند قبر أمه بما يدعو لهما
From Abd Allah ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Asamm, from Hariz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Abd Allah, who said that the Commander of the Faithful said,
"Visit your dead, for they rejoice at your visiting them. Let each of you seek his need at the grave of his father and at the grave of his mother by praying for them."

quotes.caption: Samaa and the deceased Imam, in al-Saffar, Basa'ir al-Darajat, p. 295

paragraphs.text: (4) حدثنا محمد بن عيسى عن محمد بن سنان عن عمار بن مروان عن سماعة قال دخلت على أبى عبد الله ﵇ وانا أحدث نفسي فرعاني فقال مالك تحدث نفسك تشتهى ان ترى أبا جعفر ﵇ قلت نعم قال قم فادخل البيت فإذا هو أبو جعفر ﵇ قال اتى قوم من الشيعة الحسن بن علي ﵇ بعد قتل أمير المؤمنين ﵇ فسألوه قال تعرفون أمير المؤمنين ﵇ إذا رأيتموه قالوا نعم قال فارفعوا الستر فرفعوه فإذا هم بأمير المؤمنين ﵇ لا ينكرونه وقال أمير المؤمنين ﵇ يموت من مات منا وليس بميت ويبقى من بقي منا حجة عليكم .
4 - Muhammad ibn Isa related to us from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Ammar ibn Marwan, from Sama'ah, who said,

"I entered upon Abu Abd Allah while I was speaking to myself. He noticed me and said, 'What is the matter with you, speaking to yourself? Do you wish to see Abu Ja'far?' I said, 'Yes.' He said, 'Rise and enter the house.' There was Abu Ja'far."

He said, "A group of the Shi'a came to al-Hasan ibn Ali after the killing of the Commander of the Faithful and asked him, 'Will you recognize the Commander of the Faithful when you see him?' They said, 'Yes.' He said, 'Then raise the curtain.' They raised it, and there was the Commander of the Faithful, whom they did not fail to recognize. The Commander of the Faithful said, 'Whoever of us dies does not die, and whoever of us remains is a proof against you.'"

quotes.caption: The Friday-night ascent, Imam al-Sadiq, al-Kafi, vol. 1, pp. 301-302

paragraphs.text: (باب) (في أن الأئمة ﵈ يزدادون في ليلة الجمعة) 1 - حدثني أحمد بن إدريس القمي ومحمد بن يحيى ، عن الحسن بن علي الكوفي عن موسى بن سعدان ، عن عبد الله بن أيوب ، عن أبي يحيى الصنعاني ، عن أبي عبد الله ﵇ قال : قال لي : يا أبا يحيى إن لنا في ليالي الجمعة لشأنا من الشأن ، قال قلت جعلت فداك وما ذاك الشأن قال : يؤذن لأرواح الأنبياء الموتى ﵈ وأرواح الأوصياء
Chapter on the Imams increasing on Friday night.
Ahmad ibn Idris al-Qummi and Muhammad ibn Yahya related to me from al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Kufi, from Musa ibn Sa'dan, from Abd Allah ibn Ayyub, from Abu Yahya al-San'ani, from Abu Abd Allah, who said,
"He said to me, 'O Abu Yahya, on Friday nights we have an affair of great importance.'
I said, 'May I be your ransom, and what is that affair?'
He said, 'Permission is given to the souls of the deceased prophets and the souls of the legatees'

quotes.caption: The Friday-night ascent, continued, al-Kafi, vol. 1, p. 302

paragraphs.text: الموتى وروح الوصي الذي بين ظهرانيكم ، يعرج بها إلى السماء حتى توافي عرش ربها ، فتطوف به أسبوعا وتصلي عند كل قائمة من قوائم العرش ركعتين ، ثم ترد إلى الأبدان التي كانت فيها فتصبح الأنبياء والأوصياء قد ملؤا سرورا ويصبح الوصي الذي بين ظهرانيكم وقد زيد في علمه مثل جم الغفير .

of the deceased, and the soul of the successor who is among you, to ascend to heaven until they reach the Throne of their Lord. They circumambulate it seven times and pray two units of prayer at each support of the Throne. Then they are returned to the bodies in which they had been. The prophets and successors awake filled with joy, and the successor who is among you awakes with an increase in his knowledge as abundant as a vast multitude."

quotes.caption: Imam al-Sadiq to Mufaddal, al-Kafi, vol. 1, p. 302

paragraphs.text: 2 - محمد بن يحيى ، عن أحمد بن أبي زاهر ، عن جعفر بن محمد الكوفي ، عن يوسف الابزاري ، عن المفضل قال : قال لي أبو عبد الله ﵇ ذات يوم وكان لا يكنيني قبل ذلك : يا أبا عبد الله قال : قلت : لبيك ، قال : إن لنا في كل ليلة جمعة سرورا قلت زادك الله وما ذاك ؟ قال : إذا كان ليلة الجمعة وافى رسول الله ﵌ العرش ووافى الأئمة ﵈ معه ووافينا معهم ، فلا ترد أرواحنا إلى أبداننا إلا بعلم مستفاد ، ولولا ذلك لأنفدنا .
Muhammad ibn Yahya related from Ahmad ibn Abi Zahir, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Kufi, from Yusuf al-Abzari, from al-Mufaddal, who said,
"One day Abu Abd Allah said to me, though he had not previously addressed me by a kunyah, 'O Abu Abd Allah.'
I said, 'At your service.'
He said, 'Every Friday night we have joy.'
I said, 'May God increase you. What is that?'

He said, 'When Friday night comes, the Messenger of God comes to the Throne, the Imams come with him, and we come with them. Our souls are returned to our bodies only with newly acquired knowledge. Were it not for that, what we have would run out.'"

quotes.caption: Imam al-Baqir to Zurara, al-Kafi, vol. 1, p. 303

paragraphs.text: 3 - محمد بن يحيى ، عن أحمد بن محمد ، عن ابن أبي نصر ، عن ثعلبة ، عن زرارة قال : سمعت أبا جعفر ﵇ يقول : لولا أنا نزداد لأنفدنا ، قال : قلت : تزدادون شيئا لا يعلمه رسول الله ﵌ ؟ قال : أما إنه إذا كان ذلك عرض على رسول الله ﵌ ثم على الأئمة ثم انتهى الامر إلينا .
Muhammad ibn Yahya related from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Abi Nasr, from Tha'laba, from Zurara, who said,
"I heard Abu Ja'far say, 'Were we not to increase, we would run out.'
I said, 'Do you increase in something that the Messenger of God does not know?'
He said, 'Indeed, when that occurs, it is presented to the Messenger of God, then to the Imams, and then the matter reaches us.'"

quotes.caption: Imam al-Sadiq, al-Kafi, vol. 1, p. 303

paragraphs.text: 4 - علي بن إبراهيم ، عن محمد بن عيسى ، عن يونس بن عبد الرحمن ، عن بعض أصحابه ، عن أبي عبد الله ﵇ قال : ليس يخرج شئ من عند الله ﷿ حتى يبدأ برسول الله ﵌ ثم بأمير المؤمنين ﵇ ثم بواحد بعد واحد ، لكيلا يكون آخرنا أعلم من أولنا .
Ali ibn Ibrahim related from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman, from one of his companions, from Abu Abd Allah, who said,

"Nothing comes forth from God until it begins with the Messenger of God, then the Commander of the Faithful, then one after another, so that the last of us may not be more knowledgeable than the first of us."

quotes.caption: The chapter on acquired knowledge, Basa'ir al-Darajat, p. 152

paragraphs.text: (6) حدثنا أحمد بن إسحاق عن الحسن بن عباس بن حريش عن أبي جعفر ﵇ قال قال أبو عبد الله ﵇ والله ان أرواحنا وارواح النبيين لتوافى العرش ليلة كل جمعة فما ترد في أبداننا الا بجم الغفير من العلم .

Ahmad ibn Ishaq related to us from al-Hasan ibn Abbas ibn Huraysh, from Abu Ja'far, who said, "Abu Abd Allah said, 'By God, our souls and the souls of the prophets come to the Throne on every Friday night. They are returned to our bodies only with a vast abundance of knowledge.'"

quotes.caption: The chapter, continued, Basa'ir al-Darajat, p. 152

paragraphs.text: (7) حدثنا محمد بن إسحاق بن سعد عن الحسن بن عباس بن حريش عن أبي جعفر ﵇ قال قال رسول الله ﵌ ان أرواحنا وارواح النبيين توافي العرش كل ليلة جمعة فتصبح الأوصياء وقد زيد في علمهم مثل جم الغفير من العلم .

Muhammad ibn Ishaq ibn Sa'd related to us from al-Hasan ibn Abbas ibn Huraysh, from Abu Ja'far, who said, "The Messenger of God said, 'Our souls and the souls of the prophets come to the Throne every Friday night, and the legatees awaken having been increased in their knowledge by an amount like a vast abundance of knowledge.'"

quotes.caption: Imam al-Sadiq, al-Kafi, vol. 4, p. 567

paragraphs.text: 1 - عدة من أصحابنا ، عن أحمد بن محمد ، عن علي بن الحكم ، عن زياد بن أبي الحلال ، عن أبي عبد الله (﵇) قال : ما من نبي ولا وصي نبي يبقى في الأرض أكثر من ثلاثة أيام حتى ترفع روحه وعظمه ولحمه إلى السماء وإنما تؤتى مواضع آثارهم ويبلغونهم من بعيد السلام ويسمعونهم في مواضع آثارهم من قريب .
A number of our companions related from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Ziyad ibn Abi al-Hilal, from Abu Abd Allah, who said,

"No prophet or legatee of a prophet remains in the earth for more than three days before his soul, bones, and flesh are raised to heaven. Rather, the sites of their traces are visited, greetings are conveyed to them from afar, and they hear them nearby at the sites of their traces."

quotes.caption: Imam al-Sadiq, al-Tusi, Tahdhib al-Ahkam, vol. 6, p. 106

paragraphs.text: (186) 2 - محمد بن أحمد بن داود القمي عن أبيه عن محمد بن الحسن الصفار عن أحمد بن محمد عن علي بن الحكم عن زياد بن أبي الحلال عن أبي عبد الله (﵇) قال : ما من نبي ولا وصي يبقى في الأرض بعد موته أكثر من ثلاثة أيام حتى ترفع روحه وعظمه ولحمه إلى السماء ، وإنما تؤتى مواضع آثارهم ويبلغهم السلام من بعيد ويسمعونه في موضع آثارهم من قريب .

Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Dawud al-Qummi related from his father, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Ziyad ibn Abi al-Hilal, from Abu Abd Allah, who said,

"No prophet or legatee remains in the earth after his death for more than three days before his soul, bones, and flesh are raised to heaven. Rather, the sites of their traces are visited, greetings are conveyed to them from afar, and they hear it nearby at the sites of their traces."

quotes.caption: Imam al-Sadiq, the forty-day report, in al-Tusi, Tahdhib al-Ahkam, vol. 6, p. 106

paragraphs.text: (185) 1 - الشيخ ﵀ قال : أخبرني الشريف الفاضل أبو عبد الله محمد بن محمد بن طاهر الموسوي عن أحمد بن محمد بن سعيد عن علي بن الحسن ابن فضال عن أخيه أحمد عن العلا بن يحيى أخي مغلس عن عمرو بن زياد عن عطية الابزاري قال : سمعت أبا عبد الله (﵇) يقول : لا تمكث جثة نبي ولا وصي نبي في الأرض أكثر من أربعين يوما .

Al-Tusi said, "The noble and learned Abu Abd Allah Muhammad ibn Muhammad ibn Tahir al-Musawi informed me from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Sa'id, from Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Faddal, from his brother Ahmad, from al-Ala ibn Yahya, the brother of Mughallis, from Amr ibn Ziyad, from Atiyya al-Abzari, who said, 'I heard Abu Abd Allah say, "The body of no prophet or legatee of a prophet remains in the earth for more than forty days."'"

quotes.caption: The burial of Ali, in al-Tusi, Tahdhib al-Ahkam, vol. 6, pp. 106-107

paragraphs.text: (187) 3 - محمد بن أحمد بن داود القمي قال : أخبرني محمد بن علي ابن الفضل قال : أخبرني علي بن الحسين بن يعقوب من بني خزيمة قراءة عليه قال : حدثني جعفر بن محمد بن يوسف الأزدي قال : حدثنا علي بن بزرج الخياط قال : حدثنا عمرو قال : جاءني سعد الإسكاف قال : يا بني تحمل الحديث ؟ فقلت : نعم فقال : حدثني أبو عبد الله (﵇) قال : انه لما أصيب أمير المؤمنين (﵇) قال للحسن والحسين صلوات الله عليهما : غسلاني وكفناني وحنطاني واحملاني على سريري واحملا مؤخره تكفيان مقدمه ، فإنكما تنتهيان إلى قبر محفور ولحد ملحود ولبن موضوع

Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Dawud al-Qummi said, "Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Fadl informed me. He said, 'Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Ya'qub, of Banu Khuzayma, informed me by reading it to him. He said, "Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Yusuf al-Azdi related to me. He said, 'Ali ibn Buzurj the tailor related to us. He said, "Amr related to us. He said, 'Sa'd al-Iskaf came to me and said, "O my son, do you carry hadith?" I said, "Yes." He said, "Abu Abd Allah related to me that when the Commander of the Faithful was struck, he said to al-Hasan and al-Husayn, 'Wash me, shroud me, perfume me with hanut, carry me upon my bier, and carry the rear of it; you two will suffice for its front. You will come to a dug grave, a prepared burial niche, and bricks set in place'"'"'"'"

quotes.caption: The burial, continued, Tahdhib al-Ahkam, vol. 6, p. 107

paragraphs.text: فألحداني وأشرجا اللبن علي وارفعا لبنة مما يلي رأسي فانظرا ما تسمعان ، فأخذا اللبنة من عند الرأس بعد ما أشرجا عليه اللبن فإذا ليس في القبر شئ وإذا هاتف يهتف : أمير المؤمنين (﵇) كان عبدا صالحا فالحقه الله بنبيه وكذلك يفعل بالأوصياء بعد الأنبياء ، حتى لو أن نبيا مات في المشرق ومات وصيه في المغرب لألحق الله الوصي بالنبي .

Lay me in a niche grave, set the bricks over me with clay, and lift a brick from the side of my head and see what you hear." They took the brick from beside his head after setting the clay over him, and there was nothing in the grave. Then a caller called out, "The Commander of the Faithful was a righteous servant, so God joined him to His Prophet. Thus He does with the executors after the prophets. Even if a prophet died in the east and his executor died in the west, God would join the executor to the prophet."

quotes.caption: Ibrahim al-Dizaj's account, in al-Tusi, al-Amali, p. 356, report 653

paragraphs.text: 653 / 100 - أخبرنا ابن خشيش ، عن محمد بن عبد الله ، قال : حدثنا أحمد بن عبد الله بن محمد بن عمار الثقفي الكاتب ، قال . حدثنا علي بن محمد بن سليمان النوفلي ، عن أبي علي الحسين بن محمد بن مسلمة بن أبي عبيدة بن محمد بن عمار ابن ياسر ، قال : حدثني إبراهيم الديزج ، قال : بعثني المتوكل إلى كربلاء لتغيير قبر الحسين (﵇) ، وكتب معي إلى جعفر بن محمد بن عمار القاضي : أعلمك أني قد بعثت إبراهيم الديزج إلى كربلاء لنبش قبر الحسين ، فإذا قرأت كتابي فقف على الامر حتى تعرف فعل أو لم يفعل . قال الديزج : فعرفني جعفر بن محمد بن عمار ما كتب به إليه ، ففعلت ما أمرني به جعفر بن محمد بن عمار ثم أتيته ، فقال لي . ما صنعت ؟ فقلت : قد فعلت ما أمرت به ، فلم أر شيئا ولم أجد شيئا . فقال . لي : أفلا عمقته ؟ قلت : قد فعلت وما رأيت ، فكتب إلى السلطان : إن إبراهيم الديزج قد نبش فلم يجد شيئا وأمرته فمخره بالماء ، وكربه بالبقر . قال أبو علي العماري : فحدثني إبراهيم الديزج ، وسألته عن صورة الامر ، فقال لي . أتيت في خاصة غلماني فقط ، وإني نبشت فوجدت بارية جديدة وعليها بدن الحسين بن علي ووجدت منه رائحة المسك ، فتركت البارية على حالتها وبدن الحسين على البارية ، وأمرت بطرح التراب عليه ، وأطلقت عليه الماء ، وأمرت بالبقر لتمخره وتحرثه فلم تطأه البقر ، وكانت إذا جاءت إلى الموضع رجعت عنه ، فحلفت لغلماني بالله وبالايمان المغلظة لئن ذكر أحد هذا لأقتلنه .

653/100. Ibn Hashish informed us, from Muhammad ibn Abd Allah, from Ahmad ibn Abd Allah ibn Muhammad ibn Ammar al-Thaqafi the scribe, from Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Sulayman al-Nufali, from Abu Ali al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn Maslama, that Ibrahim al-Dizaj related to him, "Al-Mutawakkil sent me to Karbala to alter the grave of al-Husayn. He wrote with me to Jafar ibn Muhammad ibn Ammar, the judge, 'I inform you that I have sent Ibrahim al-Dizaj to Karbala to exhume the grave of al-Husayn. When you read my letter, attend to the matter until you know whether he has done it or not.'"

Al-Dizaj said, "Jafar ibn Muhammad ibn Ammar told me what had been written to him. I did what he ordered me to do, then I came to him. He said to me, 'What have you done?' I said, 'I have done what you ordered me to do. I saw nothing and found nothing.' He said to me, 'Did you not dig deeper?' I said, 'I did, and I saw nothing.' So he wrote to the ruler that Ibrahim al-Dizaj had exhumed it and found nothing, and that he had ordered him to let water run over it and plow it with cattle.

Abu Ali al-Amari said, "Ibrahim al-Dizaj related to me, and I asked him about how the matter had occurred. He said to me, 'I came with only my own slave boys. I exhumed it and found a new mat, with the body of al-Husayn ibn Ali upon it. I smelled musk from him. So I left the mat as it was and the body of al-Husayn upon the mat. I ordered earth to be thrown over it and released water over it. I ordered cattle to run over it and plow it, but the cattle would not tread upon it, and whenever they came to the spot, they turned back from it. I made my servants swear by God, with solemn oaths, that if any one of them mentioned this, I would kill him.'"

quotes.caption: Sayyid Jafar Murtada al-Amili, Mukhtasar Mufid, vol. 6, p. 13

paragraphs.text: فإن رفع الأجساد إلى السماء ، ليس بالأمر الذي يصح التشكيك فيه ، بعد تصريح القرآن ، وتواتر الحديث به . . فإن معراج نبينا الأعظم بجسده وروحه ، ثابت بلا ريب ، وقد أشارت إليه آيات القرآن الكريم (1) . . والأحاديث الشريفة المتواترة . . وهذا دليل على الوقوع فضلاً عن الإمكان . . كما أن الله تعالى قد أشار إلى رفع النبي إدريس ﵇ ، إلى السماء (وَرَفَعْنَاهُ مَكَاناً عَلِيّاً) (2) . وقد صرحت الروايات بأن الله تعالى قد قبض روحه هناك (3) . . كما أن النبي عيسى ﵇ ، قد رفعه الله إليه ، كما صرحت به الآيات الكريمة . قال تعالى : (إِنِّي مُتَوَفِّيكَ وَرَافِعُكَ إِلَيَّ) وقال : (بَلْ رَفَعَهُ اللهُ إِلَيْهِ) (4) والروايات قد أكدت ذلك أيضاً (5) . .
The raising of bodies to heaven is not a matter that can properly be doubted after the Quran has stated it explicitly and reports about it have been transmitted through recurrent transmission.
The ascension of our greatest Prophet in body and spirit is established beyond doubt. The noble verses of the Quran have indicated it, as have the recurrent noble reports.
This is evidence of its occurrence, quite apart from its possibility.
God Most High has also indicated that He raised the Prophet Idris to heaven. "And We raised him to a high place." The reports have stated explicitly that God Most High took his soul there.

Likewise, God raised the Prophet Jesus to Himself, as the noble verses state explicitly. He Most High said, "I will take you in full and raise you to Me," and He said, "Rather, God raised him to Himself." The reports have also confirmed this.

quotes.caption: The same survey, continued, Mukhtasar Mufid, vol. 6, p. 20

paragraphs.text: وإذا كان الأمر كذلك ، فإن الحصول على هذا العظم لا يتناقض مع النصوص القائلة : إن أجساد الأنبياء لا تفنى ، فلعل الجسد باق ، وقد بقي معه ما دفن من أجزاء منفصلة عنه . . كالظفر ، والسن ، وما إلى ذلك . . بل إن الآيات القرآنية والأحاديث الشريفة قد دلت على أن المجرمين والطغاة كانوا يقتلون النبيين بغير حق ، وكانوا يقطعون أجسادهم بالمناشير . . فلعل هذا الجزء من ذلك الجسد الطاهر قد قطع ثم دفن . وهو لم يفن بعد . . حديث زيارة عظام آدم ويوسف : وأما بالنسبة لحديث المفضل بن عمر ، حول زيارة عظام النبي آدم ، وبدن النبي نوح ، وجسم الإمام علي ﵈ ، فنقول : أولاً : إن الحديث لا يصرح بموضع وجود تلك العظام ، وذلك البدن ، أو الجسد ، فلعلها رفعت في السماء ، لكن زيارتها في ذلك الموضع الذي كانت قد دفنت فيه توجب وصول السلام والزيارة إلى المزور عن قرب (1) ، لخصوصية في موضع الدفن . .

If this is so, then obtaining this bone does not conflict with the texts stating that the bodies of the prophets do not decay. Perhaps the body remains, along with what was buried with it of parts separated from it, such as a nail, a tooth, and the like.

Indeed, Quranic verses and noble reports indicate that criminals and tyrants used to kill the prophets unjustly and cut their bodies with saws. Perhaps this part of that pure body was cut off and then buried, and it has not yet decayed.
The report concerning the visitation of the bones of Adam and Joseph.
As for the report of al-Mufaddal ibn Umar concerning the visitation of the bones of the Prophet Adam, the body of the Prophet Noah, and the body of Imam Ali, we say the following.

First, the report does not state explicitly where those bones, that body, or that corporeal form are located. Perhaps they were raised to heaven, but visiting them at the place where they had been buried causes the greeting and visitation to reach the one visited nearby, due to a particular quality of the place of burial.

quotes.caption: The chain, al-Kafi, vol. 1, p. 580

paragraphs.text: 11 - محمد بن يحيى ، عن أحمد بن محمد بن عيسى ، ومحمد بن أبي عبد الله ومحمد بن الحسن عن سهل بن زياد جميعا ، عن الحسن بن العباس بن الجريش (2) ، عن أبي جعفر الثاني ﵇ أن أمير المؤمنين ﵇ قال لابن عباس : إن ليلة القدر في كل سنة ، وإنه ينزل في تلك الليلة

11 - Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, and Muhammad ibn Abi Abd Allah and Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, all from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from al-Hasan ibn al-Abbas ibn al-Jarish (2), from Abu Ja'far the Second, that the Commander of the Faithful said to Ibn Abbas,
"Laylat al-Qadr occurs in every year, and on that night there descends"

quotes.caption: The chain, continued, al-Kafi, vol. 1, p. 581

paragraphs.text: أمر السنة ولذلك الامر ولاة بعد رسول الله ﵌ ، فقال ابن عباس : من هم ؟ قال : أنا وأحد عشر من صلبي أئمة محدثون .
The command of the Sunna, and that command has governors after the Messenger of God. Ibn Abbas said, "Who are they?" He said, "I and eleven from my loins, Imams who are spoken to."

quotes.caption: The report of Ali and Abu Bakr, al-Kafi, vol. 1, p. 581

paragraphs.text: 13 - وبهذا الاسناد أن أمير المؤمنين ﵇ قال لأبي بكر يوما : " لا تحسبن الذين قتلوا في سبيل الله أمواتا بل أحياء عند ربهم يرزقون " وأشهد [أن] محمدا ﵌ رسول الله مات شهيدا والله ليأتينك ، فأيقن إذا جاءك فان الشيطان غير متخيل (1) به فأخذ علي بيد أبي بكر فأراه النبي ﵌ فقال له : يا أبا بكر آمن بعلي وبأحد عشر من ولده ، إنهم مثلي إلا النبوة وتب إلى الله مما في يدك ، فإنه لا حق لك فيه ، قال ثم ذهب فلم ير (2)

13 - Through this chain of transmission, the Commander of the Faithful said to Abu Bakr one day, "Do not suppose that those who have been killed in the way of God are dead. Rather, they are alive, receiving provision from their Lord." And I bear witness that Muhammad, the Messenger of God, died a martyr. By God, he will surely come to you. So be certain when he comes to you, for Satan cannot assume his appearance.

Then Ali took Abu Bakr by the hand and showed him the Prophet. He said to him, "O Abu Bakr, believe in Ali and in eleven of his descendants. They are like me, except for prophethood. Repent to God from what is in your hand, for you have no right to it." Then he departed and was not seen.

quotes.caption: Imam al-Rida, in al-Saffar, Basa'ir al-Darajat, p. 294

paragraphs.text: (5) باب في أن الأئمة ﵈ يزورون الموتى وان الموتى يزورهم . (1) حدثنا معاوية بن حكيم عن الحسين بن علي الوشا عن أبي الحسن الرضا ﵇ قال قال لي بخراسان رأيت رسول الله ﵌ هيهنا والتزمته .
(5) Chapter on the fact that the Imams visit the dead and that the dead visit them.
(1) Mu'awiyah ibn Hakim narrated to us, from al-Husayn ibn Ali al-Washsha, from Abu al-Hasan al-Rida, who said to me in Khurasan, "I saw the Messenger of God here and embraced him."

quotes.caption: The encounter at the Quba mosque, Basa'ir al-Darajat, p. 294

paragraphs.text: (2) حدثنا محمد بن عيسى عن ابن أبي عمير وعلي بن الحكم بن مسكين عن ابن عمارة عن أبي عبد الله وعثمان بن عيسى عن أبان بن تغلب عن أبي عبد الله ﵇ ان أمير المؤمنين ﵇ لقى أبا بكر فاحتج عليه ثم قال له اما ترضى برسول الله ﵌ بيني وبينك قال فكيف لي به فاخذ بيده واتى مسجد قبا فإذا رسول الله ﵌ فيه فقضى على أبى بكر فرجع أبو بكر مذعورا فلقي عمر فأخبره فقال مالك اما علمت سحر بني هاشم .

(2) Muhammad ibn Isa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Umayr and Ali ibn al-Hakam ibn Miskin, from Ibn Ammarah, from Abu Abd Allah, and from Uthman ibn Isa, from Aban ibn Taghlib, from Abu Abd Allah, that the Commander of the Faithful met Abu Bakr and argued his case against him. Then he said to him,
"Are you not satisfied to have the Messenger of God judge between you and me?"
He said, "How can I get to him?"

So he took his hand and brought him to the Mosque of Quba. There was the Messenger of God in it, and he rendered judgment against Abu Bakr. Abu Bakr returned terrified and met Umar, informing him of it. Umar said, "What is wrong with you? Did you not know the sorcery of the Banu Hashim?"

quotes.caption: The Prophet on dreams, quoted in al-Tusi, al-Amali, p. 354

paragraphs.text: فإن موضعا يأتيه إبراهيم ومحمد وجبرئيل وميكائيل (﵈) لحقيق بأن يرغب في إتيانه وزيارته ، فإن أبا حصين حدثني أن رسول الله (﵌) قال : من رآني في المنام فإياي رأى ، فإن الشيطان لا يتشبه بي .

A place visited by Abraham, Muhammad, Gabriel, and Michael is surely worthy of being desired and visited. Abu Husayn told me that the Messenger of God said, "Whoever sees me in a dream has truly seen me, for Satan cannot take my likeness."

quotes.caption: The dream warning to the commander, in al-Tusi, al-Amali, pp. 356-357, report 654

paragraphs.text: 654 / 101 - أخبرنا ابن خشيش ، عن محمد بن عبد الله ، قال : حدثني محمد ابن إبراهيم بن أبي السلاسل الأنباري الكاتب ، قال : حدثني أبو عبد الله الباقطاني ، قال : ضمني عبيد الله بن يحيى بن خاقان إلى هارون المعري ، وكان قائدا من قواد السلطان ، أكتب له ، وكان بدنه كله أبيض شديد البياض حتى يديه ورجليه كانا كذلك ، وكان وجهه أسود شديد السواد كأنه القير ، وكان يتفقأ مع ذلك مدة (1) منتنة .

654/101. Ibn Hashish informed us, from Muhammad ibn Abd Allah, that Muhammad ibn Ibrahim ibn Abi al-Salasil al-Anbari the scribe related to him, that Abu Abd Allah al-Baqatani related to him, "Ubayd Allah ibn Yahya ibn Khaqan assigned me to Harun al-Marri, who was one of the ruler's commanders, and I wrote for him. His entire body was white, intensely white, even his hands and feet were so. Yet his face was black, intensely black, as though it were tar, and he would also break out in foul-smelling pustules."

quotes.caption: The dream warning, continued, al-Tusi, al-Amali, p. 357

paragraphs.text: قال : فلما آنس بي سألته عن سراد وجهه فأبى أن يخبرني ، ثم إنه مرض مرضه الذي مات فيه ، فقعدت فسألته ، فرأيته كأنه يحب أن يكتم عليه ، فضمنت له الكتمان فحدثني ، قال : وجهني المتوكل أنا والديزج لنبش قبر الحسين (﵇) وإجراء الماء عليه ، فلما عزمت على الخروج والمسير إلى الناحية رأيت رسول الله (﵌) في المنام ، فقال : لا تخرج مع الديزج ولا تفعل ما أمرتم به في قبر الحسين . فلما أصبحنا جاءوا يستحثونني في المسير ، فسرت معهم حتى وافينا كربلاء ، وفعلنا ما أمرنا به المتوكل ، فرأيت النبي (﵌) في المنام فقال : ألم آمرك ألا تخرج معهم ولا تفعل فعلهم ، فلم تقبل حتى فعلت ما فعلوا ؟ ! ثم لطمني وتفل في وجهي ، فصار وجهي مسودا كما ترى ، وجسمي على حالته الأولى .

He said, "When I became familiar with him, I asked him about the blackness of his face, but he refused to tell me. Then he fell ill with the illness from which he died. I sat with him and asked him, and I saw that he wished to keep it concealed. So I guaranteed him secrecy, and he told me. He said, 'Al-Mutawakkil sent al-Dizaj and me to exhume the grave of al-Husayn and run water over it. When I resolved to depart and travel to that region, I saw the Messenger of God in a dream. He said, "Do not go out with al-Dizaj, and do not do what you have been ordered to do concerning the grave of al-Husayn."'

"When morning came, they came urging me to set out. I went with them until we reached Karbala, and we did what al-Mutawakkil had ordered us to do. I saw the Prophet in a dream, and he said, 'Did I not command you not to go out with them and not to do what they did? Yet you would not accept it until you did what they did.' Then he struck me across the face and spat in my face. My face became black as you see, while my body remained in its former condition."

quotes.caption: Qur'an 10:64

paragraphs.text: لَهُمُ ٱلْبُشْرَىٰ فِى ٱلْحَيَوٰةِ ٱلدُّنْيَا وَفِى ٱلْءَاخِرَةِ ۚ لَا تَبْدِيلَ لِكَلِمَٰتِ ٱللَّهِ ۚ ذَٰلِكَ هُوَ ٱلْفَوْزُ ٱلْعَظِيمُ
lahum al-bushra fi al-hayati al-dunya wa-fi al-akhirah, la tabdila li-kalimati Allahi, dhalika huwa l-fawzu l-'azim
For them is good news in the life of this world and in the Hereafter. There is no changing the words of God. That is the great triumph.

quotes.caption: Imam al-Baqir, al-Kafi, vol. 8, p. 114

paragraphs.text: 60 - عنه ، عن أحمد بن محمد ، عن ابن فضال ، عن أبي جميلة ، عن جابر ، عن أبي جعفر (﵇) قال : قال رجل لرسول الله (﵌) : في قول الله ﷿ : " لهم البشرى في الحياة الدنيا (2) " قال : هي الرؤيا الحسنة يرى المؤمن فيبشر بها في دنياه .
60 - From him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Faddal, from Abu Jamilah, from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far, who said,

"A man said to the Messenger of God, concerning the words of God, 'For them are glad tidings in the life of this world.' He said, 'It is the good dream that the believer sees and by which he is given glad tidings in this world.'"

quotes.caption: The Prophet's instruction to the blind man, Sunan al-Tirmidhi, vol. 5, p. 569

paragraphs.text: 3578 - حَدَّثَنَا مَحْمُودُ بْنُ غَيْلَانَ قَالَ : حَدَّثَنَا عُثْمَانُ بْنُ عُمَرَ قَالَ : حَدَّثَنَا شُعْبَةُ ، عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ ، عَنْ عُمَارَةَ بْنِ خُزَيْمَةَ بْنِ ثَابِتٍ ، عَنْ عُثْمَانَ بْنِ حُنَيْفٍ ، أَنَّ رَجُلًا ضَرِيرَ البَصَرِ أَتَى النَّبِيَّ ﷺ فَقَالَ : ادْعُ اللَّهَ أَنْ يُعَافِيَنِي قَالَ : « إِنْ شِئْتَ دَعَوْتُ ، وَإِنْ شِئْتَ صَبَرْتَ فَهُوَ خَيْرٌ لَكَ » . قَالَ : فَادْعُهْ ، قَالَ : فَأَمَرَهُ أَنْ يَتَوَضَّأَ فَيُحْسِنَ وُضُوءَهُ وَيَدْعُوَ بِهَذَا الدُّعَاءِ : « اللَّهُمَّ إِنِّي أَسْأَلُكَ وَأَتَوَجَّهُ إِلَيْكَ بِنَبِيِّكَ مُحَمَّدٍ نَبِيِّ الرَّحْمَةِ ، إِنِّي تَوَجَّهْتُ بِكَ إِلَى رَبِّي فِي حَاجَتِي هَذِهِ لِتُقْضَى لِيَ ، اللَّهُمَّ فَشَفِّعْهُ فِيَّ » : هَذَا حَدِيثٌ حَسَنٌ صَحِيحٌ غَرِيبٌ لَا نَعْرِفُهُ إِلَّا مِنْ هَذَا الوَجْهِ مِنْ حَدِيثِ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ وَهُوَ الْخَطْمِي

3578 - Mahmud ibn Ghaylan related to us. Uthman ibn Umar related to us. Shu'bah related to us, from Abu Ja'far, from 'Umarah ibn Khuzaymah ibn Thabit, from Uthman ibn Hunayf, that a blind man came to the Prophet and said,
"Supplicate to Allah to grant me well-being."
He said, "If you wish, I will supplicate, and if you wish, be patient, for that is better for you."
He said, "Then supplicate to Him."

He said that he instructed him to perform ablution and do it well, then to supplicate with this supplication, "O Allah, I ask You and turn to You through Your Prophet Muhammad, the Prophet of mercy. I have turned through you to my Lord concerning this need of mine, so that it may be fulfilled for me. O Allah, accept his intercession for me."
This is a hadith that is hasan, sahih, gharib. We know it only through this route, from the hadith of Abu Ja'far, who is al-Khatmi.

quotes.caption: The same du'a in al-Hakim al-Nisaburi, al-Mustadrak, vol. 1, p. 519

paragraphs.text: عن أبي جعفر المدني قال سمعت عمارة بن خزيمة يحدث عن عثمان بن حنيف ﵁ ان رجلا ضريرا أتى النبي ﵌ فقال ادع الله تعالى ان يعافيني قال إن شئت أخرت ذلك وإن شئت دعيت قال فادعه قال فأمره ان يتوضأ فيحسن الوضوء ويصلى ركعتين ويدعو بهذا الدعاء اللهم إني أسألك وأتوجه إليك بنبيك محمد ﵌ نبي الرحمة يا محمد اني أتوجه بك إلى ربك في حاجتي هذه فتقضيها لي اللهم شفعه في وشفعني فيه هذا حديث صحيح الاسناد ولم يخرجاه
Abu Ja'far al-Madani said, "I heard 'Umarah ibn Khuzaymah relate from Uthman ibn Hunayf that a blind man came to the Prophet and said, 'Supplicate to Allah Most High to grant me well-being.'"
He said, "If you wish, I will defer that, and if you wish, I will supplicate."
He said, "Then supplicate to Him."

He instructed him to perform ablution and do it well, to pray two units of prayer, and to supplicate with this supplication, "O Allah, I ask You and turn to You through Your Prophet Muhammad, the Prophet of mercy. O Muhammad, I turn through you to your Lord concerning this need of mine, so that He may fulfill it for me. O Allah, accept his intercession for me, and accept my intercession concerning him."
This hadith is sahih al-isnad; the two of them did not record it.

quotes.caption: The post-death continuation, in al-Zabidi, Takhrij Ahadith Ihya Ulum al-Din, vol. 1, pp. 542-543

paragraphs.text: وأخرج البيهقي في الدلائل والنسائي في اليوم والليلة والنميري من طريق أبي أمامة عن سهل بن حنيف عن عمه عثمان بن حنيف أن رجلاً كان يختلف إلى عثمان بن عفان ﵁ في حاجة فكان عثمان لا يلتفت إليه ولا ينظر في حاجته قال عثمان بن حنيف فشكا ذلك إليه فقال له ائت الميضأة فتوضأ ثم ائت المسجد فصل فيه ركعتين ثم قل اللهم إني أسألك وأتوجه إليك بنبيك محمد - ﷺ - نبي الرحمة يا محمد إني أتوجه بك إلى

Al-Bayhaqi, in al-Dala'il, al-Nasa'i, in al-Yawm wa-al-Laylah, and al-Numayri, through Abu Umamah from Sahl ibn Hunayf from his uncle Uthman ibn Hunayf, reported that a man used to come repeatedly to Uthman ibn 'Affan concerning a need, but Uthman would not pay attention to him or consider his need.

Uthman ibn Hunayf said that the man complained of this to him. He said to him, "Go to the place of ablution and perform ablution. Then go to the mosque and pray two units of prayer there. Then say, 'O Allah, I ask You and turn to You through Your Prophet Muhammad, the Prophet of mercy. O Muhammad, I turn through you to

quotes.caption: The continuation, concluding, Takhrij Ahadith Ihya Ulum al-Din, vol. 1, p. 543

paragraphs.text: ربي فتقضي لي حاجتي واذكر حاجتك ثم رح حتى أروح فانطلق الرجل فصنع ذلك ثم أتى باب عثمان بن عفان فجاءه البواب فأخذ بيده وأدخله على عثمان فأجلسه معه على الطنفسة فقال حاجتك فذكر حاجته فقضاها له ثم قال ما فهمت حاجتك حتى كان الساعة وما كانت لك من حاجة فسل ثم أن الرجل خرج من عنده فلقي عثمان بن حنيف فقال له جزاك الله خيراً ما كان ينظر في حاجتي ولا يلتفت إلي حتى كلمته فقال له عثمان بن حنيف ما كلمته ولا كلمني ولكن شهدت رسول الله - ﷺ - وأتاه رجل ضرير البصر فشكا إليه ذهاب بصره فقال له النبي - ﷺ - ائت الميضأة فتوضأ ثم ائت المسجد فصل ركعتين ثم قل اللهم إني أسألك وأتوجه إليك بنبيك نبي الرحمة يا محمد إني أتوجه بك إلى ربي فتجلى لي عن بصري اللهم شفعه في وشفعني في نفسي قال عثمان فوالله ما تغرقنا ولا طال بنا الحديث حتى دخل الرجل كأنه لم يكن به ضرر ورواه أيضاً الترمذي والنسائي وابن ماجة وقال الترمذي حسن صحيح غريب وأحمد وابن خزيمة والحاكم وصححه من طريق عمارة بن خزيمة بن ثابت عن عثمان بن حنيف نحوه والله أعلم .
my Lord, so that He may fulfill my need for me,' and mention your need. Then go away until I come to you."

The man went and did that. Then he came to the door of Uthman ibn 'Affan. The doorkeeper came to him, took him by the hand, and brought him in to Uthman. He seated him with him on the carpet and said, "What is your need?"
He mentioned his need, and he fulfilled it for him. Then he said, "I did not understand your need until this very hour. Whenever you have a need, ask."
Then the man left him and met Uthman ibn Hunayf. He said to him, "May Allah reward you well. He would not consider my need or pay attention to me until you spoke to him."

Uthman ibn Hunayf said to him, "I neither spoke to him nor did he speak to me. But I witnessed the Messenger of Allah when a blind man came to him and complained to him of the loss of his sight. The Prophet said to him, 'Go to the place of ablution and perform ablution. Then go to the mosque and pray two units of prayer. Then say, "O Allah, I ask You and turn to You through Your Prophet, the Prophet of mercy. O Muhammad, I turn through you to my Lord, so that my sight may be uncovered for me. O Allah, accept his intercession for me, and accept my intercession for myself."'
Uthman said, "By Allah, we had not dispersed, nor had our conversation lasted long, before the man entered as though he had never had any impairment."

It was also related by al-Tirmidhi, al-Nasa'i, and Ibn Majah. Al-Tirmidhi said, "Sound, authentic, uncommon." Ahmad, Ibn Khuzaymah, and al-Hakim also related it, and he authenticated it, through 'Umarah ibn Khuzaymah ibn Thabit from Uthman ibn Hunayf, with similar wording. Allah knows best.

quotes.caption: The second version, in al-Hakim al-Nisaburi, al-Mustadrak, vol. 1, p. 526

paragraphs.text: عن أبي أمامة بن سهل بن حنيف عن عمه عثمان بن حنيف ﵁ ان رجلا ضرير البصر أتى النبي ﵌ فقال يا رسول الله علمني دعاء ادعو به يرد الله على بصرى فقال له قل اللهم إني أسألك وأتوجه إليك بنبيك نبي الرحمة يا محمد انى قد توجهت بك إلى ربى اللهم شفعه في وشفعني في نفسي فدعا بهذا الدعاء فقام وقد أبصر

Abu Umamah ibn Sahl ibn Hunayf reported from his uncle, Uthman ibn Hunayf, that a man whose sight was impaired came to the Prophet and said, "Messenger of God, teach me a supplication by which I may call upon God to restore my sight." He said to him, "Say, 'O God, I ask You and turn to You through Your Prophet, the Prophet of mercy. O Muhammad, I have turned through you to my Lord. O God, accept his intercession for me, and accept my intercession for myself.'" He then made this supplication, rose, and was able to see.

quotes.caption: The buried person hears the footsteps, Sunan Abu Dawud, vol. 2, p. 86

paragraphs.text: 3231 - حدثنا محمد بن سليمان الأنباري ، ثنا عبد الوهاب يعنى ابن عطاء عن سعيد ، عن قتادة ، عن أنس ، عن النبي ﵌ أنه قال : (إن العبد إذا وضع في قبره وتولى عنه أصحابه إنه ليسمع قرع نعالهم
3231 - Muhammad ibn Sulayman al-Anbari related to us. 'Abd al-Wahhab, meaning Ibn 'Ata', related to us, from Sa'id, from Qatadah, from Anas, from the Prophet, who said,
"When the servant is placed in his grave and his companions turn away from him, he hears the sound of their sandals."

quotes.caption: Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani, Fath al-Bari, vol. 6, p. 352

paragraphs.text: ومن شواهد الحديث ما أخرجه أبو داود من حديث أبي هريرة رفعه وقال فيه وصلوا علي فان صلاتكم تبلغني حيث كنتم سنده صحيح وأخرجه أبو الشيخ في كتاب الثواب بسند جيد بلفظ من صلى على عند قبري سمعته ومن صلى علي نائيا بلغته وعند أبي داود والنسائي وصححه ابن خزيمة وغيره عن أوس بن أوس رفعه في فضل يوم الجمعة فأكثروا علي من الصلاة فيه فان صلاتكم معروضة علي قالوا يا رسول الله وكيف تعرض صلاتنا عليك وقد أرمت قال إن الله حرم على الأرض أن تأكل أجساد الأنبياء

Among the supporting reports for the hadith is what Abu Dawud recorded from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah, traced back to the Prophet. It includes, "Send blessings upon me, for your blessings reach me wherever you are." Its chain is authentic.

Abu al-Shaykh recorded in the Book of Reward, with a good chain, the wording, "Whoever sends blessings upon me at my grave, I hear it. Whoever sends blessings upon me from afar, it is conveyed to me."

Abu Dawud and al-Nasa'i recorded, and Ibn Khuzaymah and others authenticated, from Aws ibn Aws, traced back to the Prophet, concerning the merit of Friday, "Send abundant blessings upon me on it, for your blessings are presented to me."
They said, "O Messenger of Allah, how will our blessings be presented to you when you have decayed?"
He said, "Allah has forbidden the earth to consume the bodies of the prophets."

quotes.caption: The Prophet's answer on his body, in Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Azim, vol. 6, p. 418

paragraphs.text: قال الإمام أحمد (2) : حدثنا حسين بن علي الجعفي عن عبد الرحمن بن يزيد بن جابر عن أبي الأشعث الصنعاني عن أوس الثقفي ﵁ قال : قال رسول اللّه ﷺ « من أفضل أيامكم يوم الجمعة ، فيه خلق آدم وفيه قبض ، وفيه النفخة ، وفيه الصعقة ، فأكثروا علي من الصلاة فيه ، فإن صلاتكم معروضة علي » قالوا : يا رسول اللّه ، وكيف تعرض عليك صلاتنا وقد أرمت ؟ يعني وقد بليت ، قال : « إن اللّه حرم على الأرض أن تأكل أجساد الأنبياء » (3) ورواه أبو داود والنسائي وابن ماجة من حديث حسين بن علي الجعفي ، وقد صحح هذا الحديث ابن خزيمة

Imam Ahmad said, "Husayn ibn 'Ali al-Ju'fi related to us, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Yazid ibn Jabir, from Abu al-Ash'ath al-San'ani, from Aws al-Thaqafi, who said that the Messenger of Allah said, 'Among your best days is Friday. On it Adam was created, on it he died, on it will be the blast, and on it will be the thunderclap. So send abundant blessings upon me on it, for your blessings are presented to me.'"
They said, "O Messenger of Allah, how will our blessings be presented to you when you have decayed?" Meaning, when you have become worn away.
He said, "Allah has forbidden the earth to consume the bodies of the prophets."
Abu Dawud, al-Nasa'i, and Ibn Majah also related it through the hadith of Husayn ibn 'Ali al-Ju'fi. Ibn Khuzaymah authenticated this hadith.

quotes.caption: Adam asks by the right of Muhammad, in Ibn Asakir, Tarikh Madinat Dimashq, vol. 7, p. 386

paragraphs.text: أخبرني رجل من أهل الكوفة من عباد الناس من الأنصار قال حدثني عبد الرحمن بن عبد ربه المازني من أهل البصرة عن شيخ من أهل المدينة من أصحاب عبد الله بن مسعود قال لما أصاب ادم الذنب نودي أن أخرج من جواري فخرج يمشي بين شجر الجنة فبدت عورته فجعل ينادي العفو العفو فإذا شجرة قد أخذت برأسه فظن أنها أمرت به فنادى بحق محمد ألا عفوت عني فخلي عنه ثم قيل له أتعرف محمدا قال نعم قيل وكيف قال لما نفخت في يا رب الروح رفعت رأسي إلى العرش فإذا فيه مكتوب محمد رسول الله (﵌) فعلمت أنك لم تخلق خلق أكرم عليك منه

A man from the people of Kufah, one of the devout worshippers among the Ansar, informed me. He said, "'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Abd Rabbih al-Mazini, from the people of Basrah, related to me from an old man from the people of Madinah, who was among the companions of 'Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud.

When Adam committed the sin, he was called, 'Leave My vicinity.' So he went out, walking among the trees of Paradise, and his private parts became exposed. He began to call out, 'Pardon, pardon.' Then a tree caught hold of his head. He thought it had been commanded concerning him, so he called out, 'By the right of Muhammad, will You not pardon me?' So he was released.
Then he was asked, 'Do you know Muhammad?'
He said, 'Yes.'
It was said, 'How?'

He said, 'When, my Lord, You breathed the spirit into me, I raised my head to the Throne and found written upon it, "Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah." I knew that You had not created any creature more honored before You than he.'"

quotes.caption: Ibn Taymiyya, Majmu al-Fatawa, vol. 1, p. 171

paragraphs.text: فَإِذَا كَانَ هَذَا مُحَرَّماً وَهُوَ سَبَبٌ لِسَخَطِ الرَّبِّ وَلَعْنَتِهِ فَكَيْفَ بِمَنْ يَقْصِدُ دُعَاءَ الْمَيِّتِ وَالدُّعَاءَ عِنْدَهُ وَبِهِ وَاعْتَقَدَ أَنَّ ذَلِكَ مِنْ أَسْبَابِ إجَابَةِ الدَّعَوَاتِ وَنَيْلِ الطَّلَبَاتِ وَقَضَاءِ الْحَاجَاتِ ؟ وَهَذَا كَانَ أَوَّلَ أَسْبَابِ الشِّرْكِ فِي قَوْمِ نُوحٍ وَعِبَادَةِ الْأَوْثَانِ فِي النَّاسِ قَالَ ابْنُ عَبَّاسٍ : كَانَ بَيْنَ آدَمَ وَنُوحٍ عَشَرَةُ قُرُونٍ كُلُّهُمْ عَلَى الْإِسْلَامِ ثُمَّ ظَهَرَ الشِّرْكُ بِسَبَبِ تَعْظِيمِ قُبُورِ صَالِحِيهِمْ .

If this is forbidden, and it is a cause of the Lord's wrath and curse, then what of one who deliberately invokes the dead, supplicates at their graves and through them, and believes that this is among the means by which supplications are answered, requests are obtained, and needs are fulfilled?

This was among the first causes of shirk among the people of Noah and of the worship of idols among people. Ibn 'Abbas said, "There were ten generations between Adam and Noah, all of them upon Islam. Then shirk appeared because of their veneration of the graves of their righteous people."

quotes.caption: Qur'an 27:80

paragraphs.text: إِنَّكَ لَا تُسْمِعُ ٱلْمَوْتَىٰ وَلَا تُسْمِعُ ٱلصُّمَّ ٱلدُّعَآءَ إِذَا وَلَّوْا۟ مُدْبِرِينَ
innaka la tusmi'u l-mawta wa-la tusmi'u l-summa l-du'a'a idha wallaw mudbirin
Indeed, you cannot make the dead hear, nor can you make the deaf hear the call when they turn away, retreating.

quotes.caption: Al-Shinqiti on the verse, Adwa al-Bayan, vol. 6, p. 122

paragraphs.text: اعلم أن التحقيق الذي دلّت عليه القرائن القرءانيّة واستقراء القرءان ، أن معنى قوله : ( إِنَّكَ لاَ تُسْمِعُ الْمَوْتَى ) ، لا يصح فيه من أقوال العلماء ، إلا تفسيران :

Know that the sound conclusion indicated by Qur'anic contextual evidence and by surveying the Qur'an is that only two interpretations of the scholars are valid regarding the meaning of His saying, “Indeed, you cannot make the dead hear.”

quotes.caption: His first reading, continued, Adwa al-Bayan, vol. 6, p. 122

paragraphs.text: الأول : أن المعنى : ( إِنَّكَ لاَ تُسْمِعُ الْمَوْتَى ) ، أي : لا تسمع الكفار الذين أمات اللَّه قلوبهم ، وكتب عليهم الشقاء في سابق علمه إسماع هدى وانتفاع ؛ لأن اللَّه كتب عليهم الشقاء ، فختم على قلوبهم ، وعلى سمعهم ، وجعل على قلوبهم الأكنة ، وفي آذانهم الوقر

The first is that the meaning of “Indeed, you cannot make the dead hear” is that you cannot make the disbelievers, whose hearts God has caused to die and upon whom He decreed wretchedness in His prior knowledge, hear in a way that brings guidance and benefit. For God decreed wretchedness for them, so He sealed their hearts and their hearing, and placed coverings over their hearts and heaviness in their ears.

quotes.caption: The second reading, and its ascription to Ibn Taymiyya, Adwa al-Bayan, vol. 6, p. 126

paragraphs.text: فهكذا الموتى الذين ضرب بهم المثل لا يجب أن ينفى عنهم جميع أنواع السماع ، كما لم ينف ذلك عن الكفار ، بل قد انتفى عنهم السماع المعتاد الذين ينتفعون به ، وأمّا سماع آخر فلا ، وهذا التفسير الثاني جزم به واقتصر عليه أبو العباس ابن تيمية

Thus, the dead who were used in the comparison need not be denied every kind of hearing, just as that was not denied of the disbelievers. Rather, they have been denied the ordinary hearing by which they benefit. As for another kind of hearing, it has not been denied. Abu al-'Abbas Ibn Taymiyya stated this second interpretation decisively and confined himself to it.

quotes.caption: Ibn Taymiyya on the story's chain, Majmu al-Fatawa, vol. 1, p. 274

paragraphs.text: قُلْت : وَقَدْ رَوَاهُ النَّسَائِي فِي كِتَابِ ( عَمَلُ الْيَوْمِ وَاللَّيْلَةِ ) مِنْ هَذِهِ الطَّرِيقِ مِنْ حَدِيثِ مُعَاذِ بْنِ هِشَامٍ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَنْ أَبِي أُمَامَةَ سَهْلِ بْنِ حَنِيفٍ عَنْ عَمِّهِ عُثْمَانَ بْنِ حَنِيفٍ . وَرَوَاهُ أَيْضاً مِنْ حَدِيثِ شُعْبَةَ وَحَمَّادِ بْنِ سَلَمَةَ كِلَاهُمَا عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَنْ عُمَارَةَ بْنِ خُزَيْمَة وَلَمْ يَرْوِهِ أَحَدٌ مِنْ هَؤُلَاءِ - لَا التِّرْمِذِيُّ وَلَا النَّسَائِي وَلَا ابْنُ مَاجَه - مِنْ تِلْكَ الطَّرِيقِ الْغَرِيبَةِ الَّتِي فِيهَا الزِّيَادَةُ : طَرِيقُ شَبِيبِ بْنِ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ رَوْحِ بْنِ الْقَاسِمِ .

I say that al-Nasa'i related it in the book Deeds of Day and Night through this route, from the hadith of Mu'adh ibn Hisham, from his father, from Abu Ja'far, from Abu Umamah Sahl ibn Hunayf, from his uncle Uthman ibn Hunayf.

He also related it from the hadith of Shu'bah and Hammad ibn Salamah, both from Abu Ja'far, from 'Umarah ibn Khuzaymah. None of these, neither al-Tirmidhi, al-Nasa'i, nor Ibn Majah, related through that uncommon route which contains the addition, the route of Shabib ibn Sa'id from Ruh ibn al-Qasim.

reuse.reason: The scope claim withholding what scripture does not grant, that no verse tells a believer to ask a deceased Imam for help, is unchanged and still bounds the reports' burden ahead of the evidence; keep carries over.

blocks.text: No verse of the Qur'an tells a believer to ask a deceased Imam for help, and the nearest texts, among them the instruction to come to the Messenger while he is alive and seek Allah's forgiveness with his prayer for them (Qur'an 4:64), concern the living. The question is whether the book and the reports together support the practice, and what exactly they support when they do. The Imams below are the twelve descendants of the Prophet through Ali and Fatima, and the corpus is the hadith literature of the school beside the Sunni books the later sections quote. Three passages supply principles. The martyrs are alive with their Lord, receiving provision (Qur'an 3:169). Allah, His Messenger and the believers see the deeds that people do (Qur'an 9:105). A servant can be granted an extraordinary capacity, and using it remains Allah's favour (Qur'an 27:40). None of these verses names a grave, a visitor, or a request.

Class: self-certification of method / fairness certification. Contribution: the first half is a usable claim (quotations complete, chains verbatim, not reconstructed); the second half praises the article's own discipline. Class: compression that blurs who taught what, when. Contribution: locates the section, but as written says the Prophet taught the du'a for post-death use, which collapses the two-step evidence (Prophet teaches it to the blind man during his life; Uthman ibn Hunayf teaches it after his death). ## Passages inspected and clean

- **Frontmatter title and summary** — factual, no performance language; the summary states findings, not method.
- **All nine headings** — each names its subject or finding; no drama, no previews.
- **Evidence index rows 1–7 and 9** — each cell carries content plus a chain observation; row 1's "without an isnad" and row 4's "both through al-Asamm" do real work.
- **Every citation title in the callouts** — bibliographic and complete; "attributed by Ibn Fahd al-Hilli" and "The second version, continued" honestly mark attribution and continuation.
- **The Qur'an section's scope-limit sentences** — "It does not state that every martyr hears every caller…", "Awareness of deeds is not yet hearing of every spoken appeal…", "The man in the verse was alive." These are necessary qualifications, not style failures.
- **The Instruction-at-the-Grave analysis** — "The addressee is Allah throughout; the Imam is asked to pray, not to grant" and "The Uddat al-Da'i formula supplies that specification, and it is the weaker chain of the two" are load-bearing distinctions with honest limits.
- **The chain-observation sentences** (al-Asamm shared route, Ibn al-Jarish, Ibn Taymiyya's single-relay dispute) and the Zurara/al-Kafi transmission-order paragraphs — substantive throughout.
- **The al-Shinqiti paragraph** — the article's crux; its two contrasts ("the hearing of guidance, not the hearing of sound"; "not contradictions to be explained away but what the canon itself affirms") carry the argument and should not be touched.
- **Closing ¶2** — "None of this weakens the reports as witnesses… All of it matters if the argument is pressed from attribution to authentication, a step the practice does not require" states a real scope conclusion once.

## Verdict

The article's substance, attribution discipline, and scope limits are strong and must survive untouched; the residual defects are a recurring layer of performance narration, self-narrated limits, defensive framing, and a recap-heavy final paragraph — all locally fixable by the rewrites above without weakening any claim.

# Reasoning review — alive-with-their-lord/candidate.md

## Answers to the six questions (with confirmations)

1. **Reports vs truth.** The register is kept almost everywhere: "in the reports," "is reported to," "as reported," "the corpus prints," and the closing's claims are scoped "in the reports." Violations are F8, F9, F10 below, plus the paraphrase slip F4.
2. **Closing over-generation.** No sentence implies all martyrs hear — the 3:169 gloss expressly denies it ("It does not state that every martyr hears every caller"), and the ordinary-believer report is bounded by "is reported to know." No sentence has the Imam granting; the article states the opposite at every joint. The actual defects run the other way: two sentences *under*- or *mis*-describe the act (F2, F3).
3. **Sunni-canon step.** The body supports the step as a chain of three: graded life-era du'a (Tirmidhi), vocative form (al-Hakim, graded), post-death application (Bayhaqi via al-Zabidi, carriers named). Ibn Taymiyya's counter is quoted verbatim, summarized accurately ("He accepts the du'a and contests the addition"), and the reply is bounded to circulation, not soundness — fair form. Defects: F4 (vocative/rak'as misattributed to Tirmidhi's text) and F6 ("gradings stand" for a story no cited grading covers).
4. **Hearing-objection answer.** The Shinqiti step is validly deployed: the exhaustiveness claim ("only two readings are sound") is attributed to al-Shinqiti, not asserted, and "Neither reading denies that the dead can hear at all" matches the quoted text. The article over-claims only in the final compressed sentence and leaves 35:22 untreated (F5).
5. **Body-question neutrality.** Genuine. Both families quoted with chains; the reconciliation labeled "his, and it is offered as an argument, not as a report"; the closing names the corpus itself as the reason the question stays open. The two departures are F7 (an incoherence, not a tilt) and F10 (a mild tilt toward the body-present side).
6. **Scope shifts.** No Imams-to-all-prophets shift: the prophet-wide claims ("no prophet or trustee," "earth forbidden to consume the prophets") are the reports' own words, quoted as such. The shifts are F9 (report → "taught by the Imams themselves"), F3 (two liturgies → "the practice"), and the title (F12).

## Findings

1. **Opening section.** "Every report below is quoted in full, with its chain as the source prints it, and each conclusion is kept to what its report carries." — Inference tested: the note's evidentiary contract. False as written: the Tahdhib ziyarah is a bounded slice of a text the dossier records as running 6:54–63, printed with no chain in the callout; the Kamil p. 206 report is marked "في حديث طويل" and carries only its core; the second Ibn Bukayr version begins mid-scene. A reader who checks one callout against this sentence will discount the rest. **Rewrite:** "Each report below is quoted as a contiguous extract, with the chain where the source prints one and a note where it prints none." (Preserves the promise of verbatim, chain-transparent citation.)

2. **The Instruction at the Grave.** "The addressee is Allah throughout; the Imam is asked to pray, not to grant." — Inference tested: what the practice is (the no-independent-power step). Contradicted by the quotation directly above it, whose vocative is "O Abu Abd Allah," and by the article's own sentences "the visitor addresses al-Husayn directly" and "The dead Imam is addressed." The needed and true claim is about the granter, not the addressee. **Rewrite:** "The grant is sought from Allah; the Imam is asked to pray, not to grant."

3. **The Instruction at the Grave (liturgies).** "The wording of these liturgies fixes what the practice is. The dead Imam is addressed, heard in the sense the reports describe, and asked to pray, while the one who grants is Allah alone." — Inference tested: scope (two quoted liturgies → "the practice") and completeness. Two problems: (a) the liturgical corpus is vast and deliberately out of the run's scope (dossier excludes Mafatih al-Jinan et al.), so two texts cannot "fix" the practice; (b) the quoted Tahdhib text itself contains "I have set down my baggage in your courtyard, seeking your protection and that of your grave" — refuge sought in the Imam and his grave, more than ask-to-pray, precisely what opponents target, and absent from the triad. The closing's "Every effect in them is sought from Allah, by the prayer of the one addressed" inherits the same under-description. **Rewrite:** "In these liturgies the Imam is addressed and asked to intercede, and the visitor also seeks refuge in him and his grave; every request for an effect ends with Allah, and no text quoted gives the Imam an independent grant." (Preserves: the structure, the refuge clause, the no-grant point.)

4. **The Same Act in the Sunni Canon.** "The blind man is told to perform wudu, pray two rak'as, and then say, O Allah… O Muhammad, I have turned through you to my Lord…" — Inference tested: question (3)'s step from "the Prophet taught a du'a addressing him." The gloss sits under the Tirmidhi callout, but the Tirmidhi text as quoted contains neither the vocative (it reads "inni tawajjahtu bika," "I have turned through you") nor the two rak'as; both are in al-Hakim's version quoted afterwards — the dossier itself records this ("Tirmidhi's own text has the second-person phrase without the vocative"). As placed, the vocative is misattributed to the graded Tirmidhi text, the exact point a critical reader checks (opponents note the sahih-graded form lacks the vocative). The evidence-table row "The Prophet's ﷺ own du'a addressing him by name, taught for use after his death" repeats the compression and also merges the life-era teaching with the post-death application. **Rewrite** the gloss to follow Tirmidhi only, then: "Al-Hakim's version adds the vocative, O Muhammad, and the two rak'as." Fix the table row to carry the vocative under al-Hakim and the post-death use under the Uthman b. Hunayf story. The inference survives intact — it rests on al-Hakim's graded text, and the article should say so there.

5. **The Hearing Objection.** "The objection, on its own school's reading, establishes only that the Prophet ﷺ could not make the disbelievers hear with benefit." (with the table row "…from Qur'an 27:80 and 35:22") — Inference tested: question (4), whether the article claims more than Shinqiti shows. Two residuals: (a) 35:22 ("those in the graves") is named as half the objection's basis and never answered; the displayed Shinqiti material treats 27:80 only; (b) the final sentence merges the two readings into one naming only "the disbelievers," but on the second reading — which al-Shinqiti reports Ibn Taymiyya confined himself to — it is the literal dead whose *beneficial* hearing is denied, so the objection survives in that form and the article does not say so. The materials to close it are already quoted (footsteps hadith, "whoever sends blessings upon me at my grave, I hear it," the blessings presented). **Fix:** after "Neither reading denies that the dead can hear at all," add: "On the second reading the objection survives only as the claim that the dead lack the hearing from which they benefit; the canon's own reports of the buried hearing sandals and of the Prophet hearing salah at his grave are that school's answer to it." For 35:22: `source-review` whether the captured Adwa slices cover it; if yes, one sentence that the same two readings govern it; if no, bound the answer ("27:80 is the proof text treated here").

6. **The Hearing Objection / closing.** "The post-death continuation of the blind man's du'a is contested by Ibn Taymiyya at one relay while its carriers and gradings stand." — Inference tested: question (3), fair form for the counter. No cited grading covers the continuation itself: Tirmidhi's hasan sahih gharib grades the du'a without the story; al-Hakim's sahih al-isnad grades the du'a; the story's carriers (Bayhaqi, al-Nasa'i, al-Numayri) transmit it. "Gradings stand" implies a standing grading of the story. **Rewrite:** "The post-death continuation is contested by Ibn Taymiyya at one relay; the carriers he names continue to transmit it, and the gradings cited apply to the du'a itself." Related, minor: "Al-Zabidi's documentation… is itself the tradition's judgment" universalizes one compiler's takhrij to "the tradition" — "the Sunni hadith literature's own record that the story circulates" is the accurate force.

7. **Their Bodies, Raised or Preserved.** "What the body texts do carry, on all sides, is that the grave is not empty of the one to whom greetings are sent…" — Inference tested: question (5), coherence of the body summary. On two of the quoted body reports the grave is precisely empty: the three-day report raises "his soul, bones, and flesh" to heaven, and the burial narrative of Ali finds "nothing in the grave." The intended point — the addressee stays reachable wherever the body is — is true and matters, but the chosen wording asserts grave-occupancy that the cited reports deny, colliding with the empty-lahd narrative printed a page earlier. **Rewrite:** "What the body texts do carry, on all sides, is that the one greeted is reachable: the three-day report itself says the greetings reach them from far away and that they hear them at the places of their traces from near." (The closing section already states the safe version; this sentence should match it.)

8. **Knowledge That Keeps Arriving.** "This is the strongest direct evidence in the corpus that the Prophet ﷺ and the earlier Imams ﵈ continue to receive information after their deaths." — Inference tested: question (1), reports vs fact. "Evidence that P" asserts P; the dossier row and the article's own frame carry "are reported to receive." **Rewrite:** "the corpus's strongest direct reports that the Prophet and the earlier Imams continue to receive information after their deaths." Otherwise this section is the note's best reasoning: the r1/r2 scope distinction is stated before the reader needs it, and the shared-transmitter observation (al-Asamm) is explicit.

9. **Seen Awake and in Dreams.** "…is the visitor's own address, taught by the Imams ﵈ themselves for the standing supplication at the grave." — Inference tested: question (6), "a report says" → "taught." The clearest instruction is chainless ("it is reported from al-Sadiq"), and the article itself says it cannot stand as sahih on this citation. **Rewrite:** "the visitor's own address, attributed to the Imams, for the standing supplication at the grave."

10. **Their Bodies (al-Dizaj gloss).** "The two versions inside one report are the report's own picture of why the corpus's body texts diverge. What is found depends on what the finder is willing to say." — Inference tested: authored inference presented as the source's frame; body-question neutrality. The report narrates two tellings; the divergence-explanation is the article's, and the maxim generalizes one story into an epistemic rule while tilting the body question toward the body-present side (official denials unreliable) on a single account. **Rewrite:** "Inside one report the public telling and the confidential one differ; the corpus's body texts may diverge the same way. This report is one instance, not a rule." (Preserves: the two-version structure and its evidentiary interest.)

11. **Opening section.** "No verse of the Qur'an tells a believer to ask a deceased Imam for help." — Inference tested: strongest unaddressed counterevidence. Strictly true as scoped to a deceased Imam, but the reader's immediate rejoinder is Qur'an 4:64 (come to the Prophet, seek Allah's forgiveness, and the Messenger prays for them), the standard proof-text for seeking the Prophet's prayer; the boundary (it concerns the living Prophet) is never drawn, and the verse appears nowhere in the note. **Fix:** one clause — "No verse tells a believer to ask a deceased Imam for help; the nearest texts, among them the instruction to come to the Prophet and seek Allah's forgiveness with his prayer for them, concern him living." Adding the verse reference needs the external-edition verification route: `source-review` before inserting a citation, or phrase it without one.

12. **Title (minor, scope).** "Alive with Their Lord - the Prophet and the Imams after Death in the Shia Reports" — the article carries a full Sunni-canon section and answers the hearing objection from Sunni tafsir and hadith; the title's scope clause is narrower than the note. **Rewrite:** drop "Shia" from the title or retitle to the survey's actual span; the frontmatter summary already describes both sides.

13. **Closing section (minor).** "…a step the practice does not require." — Inference tested: the note's central epistemic move (attribution vs authentication). For a survey, the distinction is legitimate and the disclosure supporting it is complete; but "the practice does not require" is a flat normative assertion a critical reader will pick open (a practice justified by reports arguably requires their soundness). **Rewrite:** "a step this note, as a survey of what the traditions carry, does not take," or give the reception argument one clause if the writer wants the stronger claim.

## Three strongest escape routes for a critical reader

1. **The worship/shirk objection (Ibn Taymiyya, MF 1:171).** Du'a addressed to the dead has the form of worship on his school's definitions, whatever the texts "instruct." The article quotes it, calls it "historical and serious," answers with the texts' content (ask-to-pray, grantor Allah), and defers the form-versus-belief dispute as "a separate question." Status: **bounded, not closed** — legitimate for a survey, but the phrasing "The answer to him is not to dismiss that danger but to note…" reads as disposal; mark the deferral as open. Fixing F3 matters here: if the quoted liturgy itself contains refuge-in-the-grave language, "the texts instruct asking-to-pray" no longer covers everything the visitor says, and this route widens.
2. **The hearing objection reformulated on Shinqiti's second reading, plus 35:22.** The opponent concedes 27:80 denies no hearing at all, then argues the verse (and 35:22, untreated) denies the *beneficial* hearing the practice needs. Status: **open as printed (F5)**; closable entirely from material already in the article once the loop is drawn and 35:22 is treated or bounded.
3. **The authentication gap on the load-bearing Shia texts.** The clearest instruction is chainless; the seeing-report's two routes share al-Asamm; the appearance report rides Ibn al-Jarish and Sahl b. Ziyad. Status: **closed by disclosure plus the attribution/authentication distinction** — the chain limits are printed in the table and the body, which is the survey's proper answer; the one pickable lock is the flat clause "a step the practice does not require" (F13).

## Verdict

The reasoning architecture is sound and unusually well bounded — chain limits and non-independent routes are disclosed, no all-martyrs or Imam-grants over-generation exists, Ibn Taymiyya gets fair form, and the Shinqiti step claims no more than it shows — and the remaining defects are precision failures at the joints (F1, F2, F4, F5, F6, F7), all locally fixable without touching the argument.

2. **Unscoped event assertions (Q1).** The load-bearing prose (opening, conclusion, objection handling, per-report summaries after quotes) is scoped, but five content-preview sentences assert events bare: "Deeds are presented to the Messenger ﷺ every morning, the righteous and the sinful among them, and the Imam reads this as the meaning of Qur'an 9:105." · "A companion asks Imam al-Rida ﵇ to pray for him and his household and receives the doctrine with its verse reading." · "A man cheated of his stipend asked Imam al-Hadi ﵇ to intercede, and the Imam instead taught him a supplication." · "The Prophet ﷺ taught it himself to a blind man." · "Uthman ibn Hunayf, the Companion who had witnessed the Prophet's ﷺ instruction, teaches a petitioner at Uthman's court the same supplication … and the need is met the same day." All five are quote-adjacent previews, so no reader mistakes them for independent claims, but they fall outside the article's own scoping vocabulary; the first and last are the ones worth fixing (a doctrinal event and an answered petition, the two things the article is elsewhere strictest about).

3. **Quantifier exposed by its own exhibits (liturgies paragraph and conclusion).** "Every request for an effect ends with Allah, and no text quoted gives the Imam an independent grant." — the second clause is exact; the "every" clause is exposed to the Tahdhib liturgy quoted above it ("I have set down my baggage in your courtyard, seeking your protection and that of your grave"), a request addressed to the Imam that the prose itself acknowledges two clauses earlier. The conclusion's twin, "Every effect in them is sought from Allah, by the prayer of the one addressed," is similarly exposed to the dream-warning report (the dead Prophet's strike blackens a face; nobody sought it by prayer). "Every *sought* effect" is what the article means; as printed the universal outruns its exhibits.

4. **Imprecise apposition at the Sunni section's topic sentence.** "The act they describe, addressing the Prophet ﷺ by name and seeking Allah through him, is carried by the Sunni canon as well…" — the Shia reports above describe addressing al-Husayn and Ali by name, not the Prophet; the shared act is an address to the deceased by name with a turn through him to Allah. As written, the vocative-to-the-Prophet is misassigned to the Shia reports. One-line fix at the parallelism claim's opening.

5. **Duplication (argument economy).** "The corpus reports the same awareness for ordinary dead believers, which removes the assumption that this is a doctrine invented only for Imams." (before the al-Kafi dead-believer quotes) reappears nearly verbatim after them: "The corpus reports the same awareness for ordinary dead believers; the doctrine is not reserved for the Imams." Leftover from a repositioning; keep one.

6. **Ambiguity at the shirk hinge.** "The danger his report names is real in these reports." — reads either as "the shirk danger is a real question for these reports" (intended, per the sentences after) or as "these reports exhibit the danger." At the one point where the article faces Ibn Taymiyya's strongest practical objection, the misreading should be closed off with one clause.

## Joints tested and found sound

- **Q2, hearing loop:** closed, and modestly — the article never claims the reports prove the dead hear; it shows the objectors' own school affirms dead-hearing texts. Objection → al-Shinqiti's exhaustive two readings → on reading 2 "the objection survives only as the claim that the dead lack beneficial hearing" → Abu Dawud's footsteps report plus the blessings reports Ibn Hajar and Ibn Khuzayma graded, "what the canon itself affirms." The Ibn Taymiyya-ascribed reading 2 is supported verbatim by the quote ("stated this second interpretation decisively and confined himself to it"), and "Neither reading denies that the dead can hear at all" matches it. The worship-form question is left "not settled here," which is honest, not a gap.
- **Q2, 35:22:** I verified the prose reference directly in the corpus. Adwa al-Bayan vol. 6 p. 125 (rowid 1142998) reads: "وآية (فاطر) هذه كآية (النمل) و(الروم) المتقدمتين… فلا فرق بين قوله: إنك لا تسمع الموتى، وبين قوله: وما أنت بمسمع من في القبور," and the same page opens reading 2: "المراد بالموتى الذين ماتوا بالفعل… خصوص السماع المعتاد الذي ينتفع صاحبه به." The reference is accurate and the locus correct. Note for the council: this p. 125 passage is *not* in the run's banked citations (citations.json holds only pp. 122 and 126), so it rides on my check — bank the capture.
- **Q3, Sunni split:** the argument is still carried by graded texts. Tirmidhi 3578 (hasan sahih gharib) carries the ablution-plus-supplication with the second-person turn and no vocative; al-Hakim's sahih al-isnad text carries the vocative and the two units; the article states the split three times consistently and never attributes the vocative to Tirmidhi. The post-death extension rests on the al-Zabidi-documented continuation, whose chain dispute is quoted in Ibn Taymiyya's own words with the concession "the gradings cited apply to the supplication itself" — disclosed, not hidden, and the practice claim does not depend on it.
- **Q4, closing stance:** consistent. No sentence in the article's own voice authenticates; gradings are reported as printed; limits are stated at every seam ("cannot be presented as established, graded sahih, on this citation alone"; the shared al-Asamm relay; "several versions of one encounter are not several independent confirmations"); the conclusion keeps every element "in the reports," and "removes the assumption that the practice was invented by the Shia" is calibrated as assumption-removal, not proof.
- **Q5, checked quantifiers:** "No verse of the Qur'an tells a believer…" (guarded by the 4:64 discussion), "It does not state that every martyr hears every caller," "Awareness of deeds is not yet hearing of every spoken appeal," "no text quoted gives the Imam an independent grant" — all hold against their exhibits. "The Sunni canon also affirms, in its own texts, that the dead hear" is a mild generalization but scoped by "in its own texts" and immediately evidenced; acceptable.

**Verdict:** argument-ready after fixing the one over-reaching body-texts sentence and the five one-clause precision nits; every load-bearing joint held under the final pass.

2. **Authored prose fused inside a corpus-quote callout (al-Rida promotion).** Line 97, inside the `> [!info]- Imam al-Rida ﵇ … p. 268 (continued)` callout, on the same line as the translation's last words: "Taken together, the verse and these reports support continued awareness of what the living do. Awareness of deeds is not yet hearing of every spoken appeal; that further step comes from the grave reports, not from this verse." The line begins with `>`, so the synthesis renders as part of the quote's translation — against the article's own declaration that "Each report below is quoted as a contiguous extract from its source." Move these two sentences below the callout.

3. **"Gharib" glossed one way, translated two other ways.** Line 488 prose gloss: "hasan sahih gharib, good, authentic and of a single route in his grading." Line 529, al-Zabidi callout translation: "Al-Tirmidhi said, 'Sound, authentic, uncommon.'" Line 638, Ibn Taymiyya translation: "that uncommon route which contains the addition." The reader meets "uncommon" twice with no note it is the word the prose glossed as "of a single route." Unify or state the equivalence once.

4. **Residual re-narration after the Samaa callout (line 238).** "The report then gives an earlier scene. After the killing of Ali ﵇, al-Hasan ﵇ raised the curtain for a group of Shi'a and they saw him, and the summary is Ali's own…" — the callout above already translates that scene in full. The article applies the independence caveat at the al-Asamm relay ("so the two chains are not independent confirmations of one another") and at Quba ("several versions of one encounter are not several independent confirmations of it") but not here, where the trailing sentence "The chapter's reports speak of their souls not returning to their bodies except with a great abundance of knowledge" counts them as plural. Same caveat, or cite one.

6. **"Answered in the next report" misdirects, and the next report is the same report.** Line 562: "The Companions' question, how the blessings could reach him after his body had decayed, is answered in the next report." The question and its answer ("Allah has forbidden the earth to consume the bodies of the prophets") are already inside the Fath al-Bari callout above, and the Ibn Kathir callout is the same Aws report via Musnad Ahmad — a second capture of one report, unflagged, where the article flags such duplication elsewhere. 7. **The wasi gloss overstates the renderings.** Line 242: "rendered in the translations as trustee, legatee, successor or executor." The translations contain legatee (Kafi 4:567; Tahdhib 6:106), successor (Kafi 1:302), and executor (Tahdhib burial narrative); "trustee" appears in no translation — it is the article's own prose word (line 275, "the living trustee's phrase"). Drop it from the list or mark it as the article's generic.

8. **Honorific key leaves "Abu Ja'far the Second" dangling.** Line 60 glosses "Abu Abd Allah for al-Sadiq and Abu Jafar for al-Baqir"; the Kafi 1:580 chain then prints "from Abu Ja'far the Second" with no note this is a different Imam (al-Jawad).
